claim: HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) plays an essential role in the viral life cycle by reverse transcribing the single-stranded RNA genome to a double-stranded DNA copy.
source: HIV-1 reverse transcriptase (RT) (hereinafter referred to as RT) plays an essential role in the viral life cycle by reverse transcribing the single-stranded RNA genome to a double-stranded DNA copy (Deeks et al., 2015; Engelman and Cherepanov, 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Deeks et al., 2015; Engelman and Cherepanov, 2012).

claim: HIV-1 RT has been an important target of anti-HIV therapies.
source: For this reason, it has been an important target of anti-HIV therapies (Esté and Cihlar, 2010; Gubernick et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Esté and Cihlar, 2010; Gubernick et al., 2016).

claim: NRTIs act as chain terminators and compete with incoming nucleotides in the polymerase active site.
source: There are two main types of RT inhibitors: nucleoside RT inhibitors (NRTIs), which act as chain terminators and compete with incoming nucleotides in the polymerase active site (Ren et al., 1998; Sarafianos et al., 1999; Tu et al., 2010; Yarchoan et al., 1988)
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ren et al., 1998; Sarafianos et al., 1999; Tu et al., 2010; Yarchoan et al., 1988).

claim: NNRTIs inhibit the activity of RT noncompetitively.
source: non-nucleoside RT inhibitors (NNRTIs), which inhibit the activity of RT noncompetitively (Merluzzi et al., 1990; Spence et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Merluzzi et al., 1990; Spence et al., 1995).

claim: NNRTIs bind to the non-nucleoside inhibitor-binding pocket (NNIBP) located ~10 Å from the polymerase active site.
source: NNRTIs are a group of structurally diverse compounds that bind to the non-nucleoside inhibitor-binding pocket (NNIBP) located ~10 Å from the polymerase active site (Ding et al., 1995; Kohlstaedt et al., 1992; Ren et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ding et al., 1995; Kohlstaedt et al., 1992; Ren et al., 1995).

claim: NNIBP is a hydrophobic pocket that emerges only when NNRTIs bind and induce conformational rearrangements of the residues defining the pocket.
source: NNIBP is a hydrophobic pocket that emerges only when NNRTIs bind and induce conformational rearrangements of the residues defining the pocket (Esnouf et al., 1995; Hsiou et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Esnouf et al., 1995; Hsiou et al., 1996).

claim: NNRTIs are key components in highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) due to their high specificity, desirable pharmacokinetics and generally good tolerance.
source: NNRTIs are key components in highly active antiretroviral therapy (HAART) due to their high specificity, desirable pharmacokinetics and generally good tolerance (Moore and Chaisson, 1999; Pomerantz and Horn, 2003).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Moore and Chaisson, 1999; Pomerantz and Horn, 2003).

claim: The effectiveness of NNRTIs is compromised by the emergence of drug-resistant mutations in RT.
source: Despite the success of NNRTIs in suppressing HIV-1 replication and reducing viral loads, their effectiveness is compromised by the emergence of drug-resistant mutations in RT (Wainberg et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Wainberg et al., 2011).

claim: Earlier NNRTIs, including nevirapine (NVP), delavirdine (DLV) and efavirenz (EFV), have low genetic barriers for resistance and are extremely susceptible to mutations in the NNIBP of RT.
source: Earlier NNRTIs, including nevirapine (NVP), delavirdine (DLV) and efavirenz (EFV), have low genetic barriers for resistance and are extremely susceptible to mutations in the NNIBP of RT (Das and Arnold, 2013a, 2013b).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Das and Arnold, 2013a, 2013b).

claim: K103N, Y181C and Y188L are among the most prevalent NNRTI-resistant mutations identified in RT.
source: K103N, Y181C and Y188L are among the most prevalent NNRTI-resistant mutations identified in RT (de Béthune, 2010; Wensing et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (de Béthune, 2010; Wensing et al., 2017).

claim: Y181C and Y188L mutations introduce steric hindrances between NNRTIs and the pocket, and/or eliminate critical π-π stacking interactions between side chains of the two tyrosine residues and the aromatic rings in NNRTIs.
source: Y181C and Y188L mutations introduce steric hindrances between NNRTIs and the pocket, and/or eliminate critical π-π stacking interactions between side chains of the two tyrosine residues and the aromatic rings in NNRTIs (Hsiou et al., 1998; Ren et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Hsiou et al., 1998; Ren et al., 2001).

claim: The K103N mutation was long believed to prevent the entry of NNRTIs by stabilizing the closed conformation of NNIBP.
source: As to the K103N mutation, it was long believed that it prevented the entry of NNRTIs by stabilizing the closed conformation of NNIBP (Hsiou et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Hsiou et al., 2001).

claim: A more recent study indicates that the resistance caused by K103N is more likely caused by the electrostatic difference between Asn103 and Lys103.
source: However, a more recent study indicates that the resistance is more likely caused by the electrostatic difference between Asn103 and Lys103 (Lai et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Lai et al., 2016).

claim: The K103N mutation utilizes the same mechanism as Y181C and Y188L to confer resistance to NNRTIs: by altering the shape or surface property of the NNIBP.
source: In the light of this new piece of data, the K103N mutation seems to utilize the same mechanism as Y181C and Y188L do to confer resistance to NNRTIs: by altering the shape or surface property of the NNIBP.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the cited study (Lai et al., 2016) mentioned in the preceding sentence.

claim: Next-generation NNRTIs are designed with conformational flexibility and positional adaptability and are able to target the NNIBPs of an array of drug-resistant RT mutants.
source: Next-generation NNRTIs are designed with conformational flexibility and positional adaptability and are able to target the NNIBPs of an array of drug-resistant RT mutants (Das et al., 2008, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Das et al., 2008, 2004).

claim: Etravirine (ETR) and rilpivirine (RPV) are two U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved second-generation NNRTIs belonging to the diarylpyrimidine (DAPY) family.
source: Etravirine (ETR, also known as TMC125) and rilpivirine (RPV, also known as TMC278) are two U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved second-generation NNRTIs belonging to the diarylpyrimidine (DAPY) family (Figure 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and illustrated in Figure 1.

claim: ETR and RPV show potent antiviral activities against wild-type (WT) HIV-1 and many HIV-1 variants displaying significant resistance to first-generation NNRTIs.
source: Both drugs show potent antiviral activities against wild-type (WT) HIV-1 and many HIV-1 variants displaying significant resistance to first-generation NNRTIs (Janssen et al., 2005; Ludovici et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Janssen et al., 2005; Ludovici et al., 2001).

claim: Some existing resistance-associated RT mutations, such as K101P and Y181I, can cause substantial decreases in susceptibility to ETR and RPV.
source: However, some existing resistance-associated RT mutations, such as K101P and Y181I, can still cause substantial decreases in susceptibility to ETR and RPV (Azijn et al., 2010; Giacobbi and Sluis-Cremer, 2017; Smith et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Azijn et al., 2010; Giacobbi and Sluis-Cremer, 2017; Smith et al., 2016).

claim: New resistant mutations can arise from prolonged use of ETR and RPV, which undermine their anti-HIV-1 activities.
source: Besides, new resistant mutations can arise from prolonged use of ETR and RPV, which undermine their anti-HIV-1 activities (Wensing et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Wensing et al., 2017).

claim: In patients who failed ETR- or RPV-based therapies, E138K/Q/R are among the most frequently occurred mutations identified in RT.
source: In patients who failed ETR- or RPV-based therapies, E138K/Q/R are among the most frequently occurred mutations identified in RT (Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Xu et al., 2013).

claim: Compound K-5a2 features a thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine central ring, and replaces the cyanophenyl right wing of ETR with a more extended piperidine-linked benzenesulfonamide group, while keeping the 4-cyano-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure in the left wing of ETR.
source: Compound K-5a2 features a thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine central ring, and replaces the cyanophenyl right wing of ETR with a more extended piperidine-linked benzenesulfonamide group, while keeping the 4-cyano-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure in the left wing of ETR.
evidence: The claim describes the chemical structure of K-5a2 as designed and synthesized by the authors.

claim: Compound 25a shares the same central ring and right wing structures with K-5a2, but grafts the 4-cyanovinyl-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure of RPV onto its left wing.
source: Compound 25a shares the same central ring and right wing structures with K-5a2, but grafts the 4-cyanovinyl-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure of RPV onto its left wing.
evidence: The claim describes the chemical structure of 25a as designed and synthesized by the authors.

claim: Compared with ETR, compound K-5a2 displays much lower cytotoxicity and increased anti-HIV-1 potency against WT virus and virus strains with a variety of NNRTI-resistant mutations, except K103N and K103N/Y181C.
source: Compared with ETR, compound K-5a2 displays much lower cytotoxicity and increased anti-HIV-1 potency against WT virus and virus strains with a variety of NNRTI-resistant mutations, except K103N and K103N/Y181C (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors (Kang et al., 2016).

claim: Compound 25a is exceptionally potent in inhibiting WT HIV-1 and exhibits significantly better anti-HIV-1 activities than ETR against all of the tested NNRTI-resistant HIV-1 strains in cellular assays.
source: The further optimized compound 25a is exceptionally potent in inhibiting WT HIV-1 and exhibits significantly better anti-HIV-1 activities than ETR against all of the tested NNRTI-resistant HIV-1 strains in cellular assays (Kang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work by the authors (Kang et al., 2017).

claim: 25a is superior to RPV in inhibiting RT bearing a wide range of resistance mutations, including K101P, Y181I and K103N/Y181I.
source: In this study, we demonstrated that 25a is superior to RPV in inhibiting RT bearing a wide range of resistance mutations, including K101P, Y181I and K103N/Y181I, against which RPV loses considerable potency
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Table 2, Figure 4).

claim: Crystal structures of WT and mutant RTs in complex with either K-5a2 or 25a were determined.
source: and determined the crystal structures of WT and mutant RTs in complex with either K-5a2 or 25a.
evidence: The claim is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript (Supplementary file 1, Figures 2-3).

claim: The structures illustrate the detailed interactions between RT and the two inhibitors, and explain why K-5a2 and 25a are resilient to NNRTI-resistant mutations in the NNIBP.
source: These structures illustrate the detailed interactions between RT and the two inhibitors, and explain why K-5a2 and 25a are resilient to NNRTI-resistant mutations in the NNIBP.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures determined in this study.

claim: Comparison of the binding modes of K-5a2 and 25a with those of ETR and RPV suggests the possible mechanisms for the susceptibilities of ETR and RPV to E138K and K101P mutations.
source: Additionally, comparison of the binding modes of K-5a2 and 25a with those of ETR and RPV suggests the possible mechanisms for the susceptibilities of ETR and RPV to E138K and K101P mutations.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison and inference from the crystal structures.

claim: The complexes of 25a or K-5a2 bound to WT RT or RT variants with drug-resistant mutations were prepared by soaking either NNRTI into the RT crystals.
source: The complexes of 25a or K-5a2 bound to WT RT or RT variants with drug-resistant mutations were prepared by soaking either NNRTI into the RT crystals.
evidence: The claim describes the experimental method used to prepare the complexes.

claim: The structures were determined by molecular replacement using the structure of WT RT/RPV complex (PDB ID: 4G1Q) as the search template and were subsequently refined to 1.9–2.23 Å resolution.
source: The structures were determined by molecular replacement using the structure of WT RT/RPV complex (PDB ID: 4G1Q) as the search template and were subsequently refined to 1.9–2.23 Å resolution (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim describes the method used for structure determination and is supported by data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The structure of RT in the complexes has the same 'open-cleft' conformation as observed in prior RT/NNRTIs structures.
source: Overall, the structure of RT in the complexes has the same 'open-cleft' conformation as observed in prior RT/NNRTIs structures (Figure 2A and C) (Das et al., 2008, 2004; Ding et al., 1995; Ren et al., 1995).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 2A and C and citations to prior work.

claim: The Fo-Fc electron-density maps unambiguously defined the binding positions and conformations of both inhibitors in the NNIBP.
source: The Fo-Fc electron-density maps unambiguously defined the binding positions and conformations of both inhibitors in the NNIBP (Figure 2B and D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by electron density maps shown in Figure 2B and D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The RT-bound 25a and K-5a2 adopt a horseshoe conformation, which is similar to that seen with NNRTIs in the DAPY family.
source: The RT-bound 25a and K-5a2 adopt a horseshoe conformation, which is similar to that seen with NNRTIs in the DAPY family (Das et al., 2008, 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data and citations to prior work (Das et al., 2008, 2004).

claim: Both inhibitors exhibit remarkable structural complementarity to the NNIBP with substantial extensions into the three channels (tunnel, entrance and groove) characterizing the pocket.
source: Both inhibitors exhibit remarkable structural complementarity to the NNIBP with substantial extensions into the three channels (tunnel, entrance and groove) characterizing the pocket (Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural data shown in Figure 3A and B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: The left wing structures of 25a and K-5a2 form hydrophobic interactions with Pro95 and Leu234, and project into the tunnel lined by Tyr181, Tyr188, Phe227, and Trp229, forming π-π interactions with these residues.
source: The left wing structures of 25a and K-5a2 form hydrophobic interactions with Pro95 and Leu234, and project into the tunnel lined by Tyr181, Tyr188, Phe227, and Trp229, forming π-π interactions with these residues.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: By substituting the central pyrimidine ring of DAPY NNRTIs to a thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine heterocyclic structure, 25a and K-5a2 are able to establish nonpolar interactions with the alkyl chain of Glu138, while retaining the favorable hydrophobic contacts with Val179 and Leu100 manifested in the complexes of RT with ETR or RPV.
source: By substituting the central pyrimidine ring of DAPY NNRTIs to a thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine heterocyclic structure, 25a and K-5a2 are able to establish nonpolar interactions with the alkyl chain of Glu138, while retaining the favorable hydrophobic contacts with Val179 and Leu100 manifested in the complexes of RT with ETR or RPV (Das et al., 2008, 2004).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and comparison with prior structures (Das et al., 2008, 2004).

claim: The piperidine-linked aryl structure of the right wing arches into the groove surrounded by Lys103, Val106, Pro225, Phe227, Pro236, and Tyr318, developing numerous van der Waals contacts with their lipophilic side chains, and directs the terminal sulfonamide group to the solvent-exposed surface of RT.
source: The piperidine-linked aryl structure of the right wing arches into the groove surrounded by Lys103, Val106, Pro225, Phe227, Pro236, and Tyr318, developing numerous van der Waals contacts with their lipophilic side chains, and directs the terminal sulfonamide group to the solvent-exposed surface of RT.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: The surface-positioned sulfonamide group is double-hydrogen bonded with the carbonyl oxygen of Lys104 and the backbone nitrogen of Val106.
source: (i) the surface-positioned sulfonamide group is double-hydrogen bonded with the carbonyl oxygen of Lys104 and the backbone nitrogen of Val106;
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: The piperidine nitrogen forms hydrogen bonds with the main chains of Lys103 and Pro236 through a bridging water molecule.
source: (ii) the piperidine nitrogen forms hydrogen bonds with the main chains of Lys103 and Pro236 through a bridging water molecule;
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: The amine group linking the central thiophene pyrimidine and the piperidine ring interacts with the carbonyl oxygen of Lys101, forming a conserved hydrogen bond observed in a number of second-generation NNRTIs/RT complexes.
source: (iii) the amine group linking the central thiophene pyrimidine and the piperidine ring interacts with the carbonyl oxygen of Lys101, forming a conserved hydrogen bond observed in a number of second-generation NNRTIs/RT complexes (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010);
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and comparison with prior structures (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010).

claim: The nitrogen and sulfur atoms in the central thiophene pyrimidine ring are involved in two water-mediated hydrogen bonds with the backbone nitrogen of Lys101 and the carbonyl oxygens of Glu138, respectively.
source: (iv) additionally, the nitrogen and sulfur atoms in the central thiophene pyrimidine ring are involved in two water-mediated hydrogen bonds with the backbone nitrogen of Lys101 and the carbonyl oxygens of Glu138, respectively.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: These extensive interactions between the two piperidine-substituted thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine NNRTIs and RT lock the enzyme in an open-cleft conformation and inhibit its polymerization activity.
source: These extensive interactions between the two piperidine-substituted thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine NNRTIs and RT lock the enzyme in an open-cleft conformation and inhibit its polymerization activity.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the structural data and established knowledge of NNRTI mechanism.

claim: K-5a2 displays ~3-fold greater efficacy than ETR against the WT HIV-1 strain.
source: Our previous MT-4 cell-based antiviral activity evaluations showed that K-5a2 displays ~3-fold greater efficacy than ETR against the WT HIV-1 strain
evidence: The claim is supported by prior experimental data from the authors' previous work (Kang et al., 2016).

claim: K-5a2 displays higher or similar efficacy than ETR against virus variants bearing four prevalent single-residue mutations (L100I, K103N, E138K and Y181C) in RT.
source: and higher or similar efficacy against virus variants bearing four prevalent single-residue mutations (L100I, K103N, E138K and Y181C) in RT (hereinafter referred to as L100I RT, K103N RT, E138K RT and Y181C RT, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by prior experimental data from the authors' previous work (Kang et al., 2016).

claim: K-5a2 is less effective than ETR in inhibiting HIV-1 strains containing K103N/Y181C RT.
source: However, K-5a2 is less effective than ETR in inhibiting HIV-1 strains containing K103N/Y181C RT (Kang et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by prior experimental data from the authors' previous work (Kang et al., 2016).

claim: Compound 25a exhibits significantly better inhibitory effects on all tested HIV-1 strains compared to K-5a2.
source: The compound 25a, resulting from further optimization of K-5a2, overcomes the limitations of K-5a2 and exhibits significantly better inhibitory effects on all tested HIV-1 strains (Kang et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by prior experimental data from the authors' previous work (Kang et al., 2017).

claim: 25a holds advantages over RPV in most of the tested drug-resistant HIV-1 strains while retaining similar antiviral potency against HIV-1 strains containing WT RT.
source: 25a holds advantages over RPV in most of the tested drug-resistant HIV-1 strains while retaining similar antiviral potency against HIV-1 strains containing WT RT (Table 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 1.

claim: The K103N/Y181C double-mutation causes a ~4.6-fold change in susceptibility to 25a, whereas it reduces the anti-HIV-1 efficacy of RPV by more than 10-fold.
source: It is noteworthy that the particularly challenging K103N/Y181C double-mutation only causes a ~4.6-fold change in susceptibility to 25a, whereas it reduces the anti-HIV-1 efficacy of RPV by more than 10-fold.
evidence: The claim is based on data presented in Table 1.

claim: K103N/Y181C mutation confers lower level of resistance to 25a (7.2-fold change in the IC50 value) than to RPV (15-fold change) in the in vitro RT inhibition assay.
source: The superiority of 25a over RPV in targeting K103N/Y181C RT was further validated in the in vitro RT inhibition assay using purified recombinant RT variants, where K103N/Y181C mutation confers lower level of resistance to 25a (7.2-fold change in the IC50 value) than to RPV (15-fold change) (Figure 4A and B and Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4A and B and Table 2.

claim: 25a is more resilient to Y188L and V106A/F227L mutations (0.70- and 1.7-fold change, respectively) than RPV (2.2- and 4.0-fold change, respectively).
source: While 25a and RPV exhibit similar inhibitory potency against WT RT, 25a is more resilient to Y188L and V106A/F227L mutations (0.70- and 1.7-fold change, respectively) than RPV (2.2- and 4.0-fold change, respectively) (Figure 4A and B and Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4A and B and Table 2.

claim: K101P, Y181I and K103N/Y181I mutations dramatically lower the anti-RT potency of RPV and cause 20-fold, 90-fold and 1805-fold change in the IC50 values, respectively.
source: As expected, all three mutations dramatically lower the anti-RT potency of RPV and cause 20-fold, 90-fold and 1805-fold change in the IC50 values, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: There is considerably less resistance to 25a for K101P, Y181I and K103N/Y181I RT mutants (1.3-, 8.8- and 96-fold, respectively) compared to RPV.
source: In contrast, there is considerably less resistance to 25a for all three RT mutants (1.3-, 8.8- and 96-fold, respectively) (Figure 4C and D and Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4C and D and Table 2.

claim: The potency of 25a was not negatively affected by either P225H or P236L mutations (0.58- and 0.60-fold change, respectively).
source: Like that of RPV, the potency of 25a was not negatively affected by either P225H or P236L mutations (0.58- and 0.60-fold change, respectively) (Figure 4E and F and Table 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 4E and F and Table 2.

claim: 25a has a relatively high genetic barrier to the development of novel drug-resistant mutations.
source: indicating that 25a has a relatively high genetic barrier to the development of novel drug-resistant mutations.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the data showing that P225H and P236L mutations do not reduce 25a potency.

claim: 25a has steeper dose-response curve slopes than RPV in the inhibition of all tested RT variants.
source: It is worth mentioning that 25a has steeper dose-response curve slopes than RPV in the inhibition of all above RT variants (Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in Table 2.

claim: Steeper dose-response curve slopes can help 25a achieve greater inhibition of RT activity at higher than IC50 concentrations, which are usually more clinically relevant.
source: This characteristic can help 25a achieve greater inhibition of RT activity at higher than IC50 concentrations, which are usually more clinically relevant (Shen et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the data and supported by a citation (Shen et al., 2008).

claim: 25a has an improved resistance profile over RPV and is able to effectively inhibit the RT mutants causing high-level resistance to RPV.
source: Taken together, by comparing the inhibitory potency of 25a and RPV in a wide range of RT mutants, we have shown that 25a has an improved resistance profile over RPV and is able to effectively inhibit the RT mutants causing high-level resistance to RPV.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Crystal structures of K103N RT, E138K RT, and Y188L RT complexed with compound K-5a2 were determined.
source: To shed light on the mechanism underlying the outstanding resistance profile of the two piperidine-substituted thiophene[3,2-d]pyrimidine NNRTIs, we determined the crystal structures of K103N RT, E138K RT, and Y188L RT complexed with compound K-5a2
evidence: The claim is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Crystal structures of K103N RT, E138K RT, K103N/Y181C RT, V106A/F227L RT, K101P RT, and Y181I RT complexed with 25a were determined.
source: as well as K103N RT, E138K RT, K103N/Y181C RT, V106A/F227L RT, K101P RT, and Y181I RT complexed with 25a.
evidence: The claim is supported by the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Superposition of mutant RT/NNRTI complexes structures onto their respective WT RT/NNRTI complexes structures shows no major deviation in the conformations of the enzyme and inhibitors.
source: Superposition of these mutant RT/NNRTI complexes structures onto their respective WT RT/NNRTI complexes structures shows no major deviation in the conformations of the enzyme and inhibitors (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Root-mean-square deviations (RMSDs) for the structural alignments between WT RT/NNRTI complexes and mutant RT/NNRTI complexes range from 0.094 to 0.283 Å for the overall Cα atoms, and from 0.095 to 1.108 Å for the Cα atoms of the NNIBP regions.
source: Root-mean-square deviations (RMSDs) for the structural alignments between WT RT/NNRTI complexes and mutant RT/NNRTI complexes range from 0.094 to 0.283 Å for the overall Cα atoms, and from 0.095 to 1.108 Å for the Cα atoms of the NNIBP regions (residues 98–110, 178–190, 226–240 of the p66 subunit, plus residues 137–139 of the p51 subunit) (Table 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis data presented in Table 3.

claim: All the hydrogen bonds depicted in Figure 3D are preserved in the RT mutant complexes, although there are some variations in the bond lengths.
source: Examination of the interactions between the RT mutants and the two NNRTIs reveals that all the hydrogen bonds depicted in Figure 3D are preserved, although there are some variations in the bond lengths.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the crystal structures.

claim: In the structures of K103N RT in complex with 25a or K-5a2, the Lys to Asn substitution in RT shortens the aliphatic side chain and reduces the contact interface between residue 103 and the inhibitors, but 25a and K-5a2 are able to establish more contacts with Phe227 and Pro236 by varying their multiple torsion angles to counterbalance the loss.
source: In the structures of K103N RT in complex with 25a or K-5a2, the Lys to Asn substitution in RT shortens the aliphatic side chain and reduces the contact interface between residue 103 and the inhibitors, but 25a and K-5a2 are able to establish more contacts with Phe227 and Pro236 by varying their multiple torsion angles (Table 5) to counterbalance the loss (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1A, and Table 5.

claim: In the structure of Y188L RT/K-5a2 complex, the cyano-dimethylphenyl group in K-5a2 is diverted away from Leu188 to avoid steric clashes, leading to declines in the buried areas between the inhibitor and Leu188 and Phe227, but this mutation-caused damage is alleviated by its enhanced interactions with Lys103, Val106 and Pro236.
source: Similarly, in the structure of Y188L RT/K-5a2 complex, the cyano-dimethylphenyl group in K-5a2 is diverted away from Leu188 to avoid steric clashes, leading to declines in the buried areas between the inhibitor and Leu188 and Phe227. However, this mutation-caused damage is alleviated by its enhanced interactions with Lys103, Val106 and Pro236 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C, Table 4).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C and Table 4.

claim: In the case of E138K RT, since the mutation does not disrupt the hydrophobic interactions between the inhibitors' central thiophene ring and residue 138, 25a and K-5a2 maintain almost the same binding poses in the NNIBP and similar buried areas with each of the residues along the pocket as in their complexes with WT RT.
source: In the case of E138K RT, since the mutation does not disrupt the hydrophobic interactions between the inhibitors' central thiophene ring and residue 138, 25a and K-5a2 maintain almost the same binding poses in the NNIBP and similar buried areas with each of the residues along the pocket as in their complexes with WT RT (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In RT carrying the K103N/Y181C double-mutation, Y181C mutation abolishes the favorable π–π stacking interactions between the Tyr181 side chain and the dimethylphenyl ring of 25a, and greatly reduce the binding interface between 25a and Cys181.
source: In regard to RT carrying the more disruptive K103N/Y181C double-mutation, Y181C mutation abolishes the favorable π–π stacking interactions between the Tyr181 side chain and the dimethylphenyl ring of 25a, and greatly reduce the binding interface between 25a and Cys181.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the K103N/Y181C RT/25a complex structure.

claim: The markedly weakened interactions between 25a and both mutated residues in K103N/Y181C RT are remedied by the increase in the contact areas between 25a and several other residues in the NNIBP, including Tyr183, Phe227 and Pro236.
source: Nonetheless, the markedly weakened interactions between 25a and both mutated residues are remedied by the increase in the contact areas between 25a and several other residues in the NNIBP, including Tyr183, Phe227 and Pro236. (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: In the V106A/F227L RT/25a complex structure, the much smaller side chain of Ala106 buries significantly less surface area with the inhibitor.
source: In the V106A/F227L RT/25a complex structure, the much smaller side chain of Ala106 buries significantly less surface area with the inhibitor.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the V106A/F227L RT/25a complex structure.

claim: The V106A/F227L double-mutation causes more dramatic changes in the conformations of the NNIBP and the bound 25a, with the cyanovinyl group of 25a flipped so that it can maintain similar extent of interactions with the mutated Leu227.
source: Furthermore, the double-mutation causes more dramatic changes in the conformations of the NNIBP and the bound 25a. In particular, the cyanovinyl group of 25a is flipped so that it can maintain similar extent of interactions with the mutated Leu227.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the V106A/F227L RT/25a complex structure.

claim: The torsional change in 25a caused by V106A/F227L mutation diverts the inhibitor away from the tunnel lined by Tyr181, Tyr183 and Tyr188 and diminishes the contact areas between 25a and all three tyrosine residues.
source: This torsional change, however, diverts the inhibitor away from the tunnel lined by Tyr181, Tyr183 and Tyr188 and diminishes the contact areas between 25a and all three tyrosine residues.

claim: To compensate for the loss of interactions with tyrosine residues in V106A/F227L RT, the right wing of 25a shifts closer to Lys101, shortening the distance between the linker amine group of 25a and the carboxyl oxygen of Lys101 from 3.05 to 2.76 Å and strengthening the hydrogen bond between them.
source: To compensate for the loss, the right wing of 25a shifts closer to Lys101. Such movement shortens the distance between the linker amine group of 25a and the carboxyl oxygen of Lys101 from 3.05 to 2.76 Å and strengthens the hydrogen bond between them (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The hydrogen bond between the linker amine group and the carboxyl oxygen of Lys101 is conserved in the binding of many NNRTIs, including ETR and RPV, and contributes greatly to the binding affinities of NNRTIs.
source: This hydrogen bond is conserved in the binding of many NNRTIs, including ETR and RPV, and contributes greatly to the binding affinities of NNRTIs (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior work (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010).

claim: In K101P RT, the deprotonation of Pro101 main-chain nitrogen attenuates its water-mediated hydrogen bond with the pyrimidine nitrogen in 25a.
source: With respect to K101P RT, the deprotonation of Pro101 main-chain nitrogen attenuates its water-mediated hydrogen bond with the pyrimidine nitrogen in 25a.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the K101P RT/25a complex structure.

claim: The Lys to Pro substitution in K101P RT places its cyclic side chain in the vicinity of the central thiophene pyrimidine ring of 25a and leads to enhanced hydrophobic interactions.
source: Nonetheless, the Lys to Pro substitution places its cyclic side chain in the vicinity of the central thiophene pyrimidine ring of 25a and leads to enhanced hydrophobic interactions (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: In the Y181I RT/25a complex structure, the mutation not only removes the π-π stacking interactions in the left wing of 25a, but also introduces steric hinderance with the linker oxygen and thiophene sulfur group in 25a, which pushes the inhibitor slightly away from the tunnel.
source: As to the Y181I RT/25a complex structure, the mutation not only removes the π-π stacking interactions in the left wing of 25a, but also introduces steric hinderance with the linker oxygen and thiophene sulfur group in 25a, which pushes the inhibitor slightly away from the tunnel.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the Y181I RT/25a complex structure.

claim: The unfavorable change in the NNIBP caused by Y181I mutation is mitigated by the enlarged contact areas between 25a and the more closely placed side-chains of Lys101 and Tyr183.
source: This unfavorable change in the NNIBP is mitigated by the enlarged contact areas between 25a and the more closely placed side-chains of Lys101 and Tyr183 (Figure 5F).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5F.

claim: In both K103N/Y181C RT/25a and Y181I RT/25a complex structures, Tyr183 moves 2.3–2.5 Å towards the inhibitor, enhancing its hydrophobic interactions with the cyanovinyl group of 25a.
source: It is noteworthy that in both K103N/Y181C RT/25a and Y181I RT/25a complex structures, Tyr183, a residue in the conserved YMDD motif at the polymerase active site, moves 2.3–2.5 Å towards the inhibitor, enhancing its hydrophobic interactions with the cyanovinyl group of 25a.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the K103N/Y181C RT/25a and Y181I RT/25a complex structures.

claim: The recruitment of Tyr183 by the cyanovinyl group of 25a is reminiscent of that observed in the structure of K103N/Y181C RT in complex with RPV, whose left wing has the same 4-cyanovinyl-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure.
source: The recruitment of Tyr183 by the cyanovinyl group of 25a is reminiscent of that observed in the structure of K103N/Y181C RT in complex with RPV, whose left wing has the same 4-cyanovinyl-2,6-dimethylphenyl structure (Das et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison with a prior structure (Das et al., 2008).

claim: In the structure of K103N RT/K-5a2 complex, Tyr183 undergoes a significant conformational change and is placed closer to the inhibitor, although it is still outside the contact radius of the cyano group in K-5a2.
source: Interestingly, in the structure of K103N RT/K-5a2 complex, Tyr183 also undergoes a significant conformational change and is placed closer to the inhibitor, although it is still outside the contact radius of the cyano group in K-5a2.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the K103N RT/K-5a2 complex structure.

claim: Superposition of the structures of WT RT/K-5a2, K103N RT/K-5a2, WT RT/25a, and K103N/Y181C RT/25a complexes reveals a gradual rotation of Tyr183 from the 'down' position in WT RT/K-5a2 complex to the 'up' position in K103N/Y181C RT/25a complex.
source: Superposition of the structures of WT RT/K-5a2, K103N RT/K-5a2, WT RT/25a, and K103N/Y181C RT/25a complexes reveals a gradual rotation of Tyr183 from the 'down' position in WT RT/K-5a2 complex to the 'up' position in K103N/Y181C RT/25a complex (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The stepwise movement of Tyr183 is likely triggered by three factors: (i) inhibitor repositioning because of the K103N mutation, (ii) loss of aromatic interactions due to the Y181C or Y181I mutation, and (iii) presence of a cyanovinyl group in the inhibitor left wing.
source: This stepwise movement of Tyr183 is likely triggered by three factors: (i) inhibitor repositioning because of the K103N mutation, (ii) loss of aromatic interactions due to the Y181C or Y181I mutation, and (iii) presence of a cyanovinyl group in the inhibitor left wing.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: Tyr183 makes the most significant contribution to the NNRTI-binding in the circumstance that all of the three factors (K103N mutation, Y181C/Y181I mutation, and cyanovinyl group) are present.
source: Tyr183 makes the most significant contribution to the NNRTI-binding in the circumstance that all of the above factors are present.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: The ability of K-5a2 and 25a to recruit Tyr183 is particularly significant for their function of inhibiting the polymerase activity, because Tyr183 is completely conserved among all HIV-1 sequences and makes direct contacts with the nucleic acid substrate.
source: The ability of K-5a2 and 25a to recruit Tyr183 is particularly significant for their function of inhibiting the polymerase activity, because Tyr183 is completely conserved among all HIV-1 sequences and makes direct contacts with the nucleic acid substrate (Das et al., 2012; Sarafianos et al., 2001).
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis and supported by citations (Das et al., 2012; Sarafianos et al., 2001).

claim: The repositioning of Tyr183 towards the NNIBP removes its important interaction with nucleic acid and destabilizes the binding of nucleic acid.
source: The repositioning of Tyr183 towards the NNIBP removes this important interaction and destabilizes the binding of nucleic acid.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: By adopting the typical horseshoe conformation, K-5a2 and 25a substantially overlap the binding sites occupied by ETR and RPV.
source: By adopting the typical horseshoe conformation, K-5a2 and 25a substantially overlap the binding sites occupied by ETR and RPV (Figure 6).
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison shown in Figure 6.

claim: The thiophene substituent in the central ring of K-5a2 and 25a extends further into the entrance channel and is proximal to Glu138 located at the opening.
source: The thiophene substituent in the central ring of K-5a2 and 25a extends further into the entrance channel and is proximal to Glu138 located at the opening.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: The positions of the left wing structures of K-5a2 and 25a are adjusted to small conformational changes of Tyr181, Tyr183 and Tyr188 to maximize the contacts with the pocket residues in this region.
source: The positions of their left wing structures are adjusted to small conformational changes of Tyr181, Tyr183 and Tyr188 to maximize the contacts with the pocket residues in this region.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: The piperidine ring in the right wing of K-5a2 and 25a slants away from the cyanophenyl plane in ETR and RPV through a ~ 90° tilt of τ4 (from 16°/10° to –71°/–79°), leading to the displacement of Tyr318 ~1 Å away from the inhibitors.
source: The piperidine ring in the right wing of K-5a2 and 25a slants away from the cyanophenyl plane in ETR and RPV through a ~ 90° tilt of τ4 (from 16°/10° to –71°/–79°) (Table 5) (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010), leading to the displacement of Tyr318 ~1 Å away from the inhibitors.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and comparison with prior structures (Das et al., 2008; Lansdon et al., 2010).

claim: Upon the binding of K-5a2 and 25a, Pro225 and Pro236, two residues sitting at the groove channel opening, are pushed apart to accommodate the benzenesulfonamide group, which protrudes to the solvent-exposed surface of the enzyme.
source: Upon the binding of K-5a2 and 25a, Pro225 and Pro236, two residues sitting at the groove channel opening, are pushed apart to accommodate the benzenesulfonamide group, which protrudes to the solvent-exposed surface of the enzyme.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis.

claim: In the structure of WT RT/ETR complex, the amino substituent of the central pyrimidine ring forms a salt bridge with the carboxyl side chain of Glu138.
source: In the structure of WT RT/ETR complex, the amino substituent of the central pyrimidine ring forms a salt bridge with the carboxyl side chain of Glu138.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the WT RT/ETR complex structure.

claim: Transplanting Lys138 from the structure of E138K RT/K-5a2 complex into the WT RT/ETR structure reveals a severe charge-charge repulsion between the amino group in ETR and the side chain of Lys138, which would destabilize the binding of the inhibitor.
source: Transplanting Lys138 from the structure of E138K RT/K-5a2 complex into this structure reveals a severe charge-charge repulsion between the amino group in ETR and the side chain of Lys138, which would destabilize the binding of the inhibitor (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: In the case of RPV, Glu138 contributes to the RT-RPV interactions by bonding Lys101 and placing it in the vicinity of the central pyrimidine ring for several critical interactions.
source: In the case of PRV, Glu138 contributes to the RT-RPV interactions by bonding Lys101 and placing it in the vicinity of the central pyrimidine ring for several critical interactions: (i) hydrophobic interactions between the pyrimidine ring of RPV and the Cε atom of Lys101, (ii) the hydrogen bond between the pyrimidine nitrogen atom and the main-chain nitrogen of Lys101, and (iii) the hydrogen bond between a linker nitrogen atom of RPV and the carbonyl oxygen of Lys101.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of the WT RT/RPV complex structure.

claim: Modeling Lys138 from the structure of E138K RT/25a complex indicates that Lys at residue 138 of the p51 subunit would shove Lys101 away from RPV, disrupting the hydrophobic interactions and weakening the two key hydrogen bonds due to the deviation of the Lys101 backbone.
source: Modeling Lys138 from the structure of E138K RT/25a complex indicates that Lys at residue 138 of the p51 subunit would shove Lys101 away from RPV. This conformational change in RT would not only disrupt the hydrophobic interactions but also weaken the two key hydrogen bonds due to the deviation of the Lys101 backbone (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is based on structural modeling shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The K101P mutation considerably reduces susceptibility to RPV.
source: The K101P mutation considerably reduces susceptibility to RPV.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Superposition of the WT RT/RPV and K101P RT/25a complex structures reveals that the K101P mutation would remove the hydrophobic interaction between the RPV pyrimidine ring and the long aliphatic side chain of Lys101, and possibly introduces steric clashes between the polar groups in the pyrimidine ring and the non-polar side chain of Pro101.
source: Superposition of the WT RT/RPV and K101P RT/25a complex structures reveals that the mutation would remove the hydrophobic interaction between the RPV pyrimidine ring and the long aliphatic side chain of Lys101, and possibly introduces steric clashes between the polar groups in the pyrimidine ring and the non-polar side chain of Pro101.
evidence: The claim is based on structural comparison and inference.

claim: Lys to Pro substitution in K101P mutation will abrogate the critical hydrogen bond between the pyrimidine nitrogen of RPV and the backbone nitrogen in RT due to deprotonated form of Pro101 main-chain nitrogen and hence its inability to act as a hydrogen bond donor.
source: More importantly, Lys to Pro substitution will abrogate the critical hydrogen bond between the pyrimidine nitrogen of RPV and the backbone nitrogen in RT due to deprotonated form of Pro101 main-chain nitrogen and hence its inability to act as a hydrogen bond donor (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and chemical knowledge shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The improved resistance profiles of 25a over RPV against other RT mutants, especially Y181I RT, Y188L RT and K103N/Y181C RT, are likely due to the bulkier substituents in its right wing and more extensive hydrogen bond interactions with NNIBP residues.
source: The improved resistance profiles of 25a over RPV against other RT mutants, especially Y181I RT, Y188L RT and K103N/Y181C RT, are likely due to the bulkier substituents in its right wing and more extensive hydrogen bond interactions with NNIBP residues.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: The π-π interactions provided by Tyr181 and Tyr188 likely make a much less contribution to the binding affinity of 25a than to that of RPV.
source: Therefore, the π-π interactions provided by Tyr181 and Tyr188 likely make a much less contribution to the binding affinity of 25a than to that of RPV.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: The higher degree of strategic flexibility of 25a (because of more rotatable bonds) can make it more effective to preserve or even enhance its interactions with other NNIBP residues when Y181I and Y188L mutations displace the left wing structure of 25a.
source: Moreover, the higher degree of strategic flexibility of 25a (because of more rotatable bonds) can make it more effective to preserve or even enhance its interactions with other NNIBP residues when Y181I and Y188L mutations displace the left wing structure of 25a.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: By virtue of their structural flexibility, K-5a2 and 25a are able to adapt to the conformational changes of RT induced by mutations in the NNIBP and optimize their complementarity with the mutated pocket by varying their multiple torsion angles.
source: By virtue of their structural flexibility, K-5a2 and 25a are able to adapt to the conformational changes of RT induced by mutations in the NNIBP and optimize their complementarity with the mutated pocket by varying their multiple torsion angles.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis of multiple RT/inhibitor complex structures.

claim: The buried areas between the inhibitors and RT are similar across WT RT and various RT mutants, suggesting K-5a2 and 25a can occupy the NNIBP of RT mutants as effectively as they bind to the pocket of WT RT.
source: As such, the buried areas between the inhibitors and RT are similar across WT RT and various RT mutants, suggesting K-5a2 and 25a can occupy the NNIBP of RT mutants as effectively as they bind to the pocket of WT RT (Table 4).
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis data presented in Table 4.

claim: Energy calculation of the K-5a2 and 25a shows that the NNRTIs in different RT-bound conformations are almost isoenergetic, indicating the conformational changes of K-5a2 and 25a induced by NNIBP residue mutations do not bring in significant strain energy penalties.
source: Energy calculation of the K-5a2 and 25a shows that the NNRTIs in different RT-bound conformations are almost isoenergetic (Table 5), indicating the conformational changes of K-5a2 and 25a induced by NNIBP residue mutations do not bring in significant strain energy penalties.
evidence: The claim is based on energy calculations presented in Table 5.

claim: Hydrogen bonding with the main chains of NNIBP residues was previously suggested as another method to design NNRTIs that can overcome the effects of drug-resistant mutations in RT.
source: Aside from structural flexibility, hydrogen bonding with the main chains of NNIBP residues was previously suggested as another method to design NNRTIs that can overcome the effects of drug-resistant mutations in RT (Zhan et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to prior work (Zhan et al., 2009).

claim: Compared with ETR and RPV, K-5a2 and 25a form considerably more hydrogen bonds between their polar groups and the main chains of residues throughout the binding pocket.
source: Compared with ETR and RPV, K-5a2 and 25a form considerably more hydrogen bonds between their polar groups (the thiophene sulfur, piperidine nitrogen and solvent-exposed sulfonamide) and the main chains of residues throughout the binding pocket.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and comparison.

claim: The extensive network of main-chain hydrogen bonds contributes substantially to the free energy of RT-inhibitor binding and is less susceptible to side chain mutations in the pocket.
source: This extensive network of main-chain hydrogen bonds contributes substantially to the free energy of RT-inhibitor binding and is less susceptible to side chain mutations in the pocket.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis and established knowledge.

claim: The more extended right wing structures of K-5a2 and 25a contact with a larger set of NNIBP residues than DAPY NNRTIs.
source: Furthermore, the more extended right wing structures of K-5a2 and 25a contact with a larger set of NNIBP residues than DAPY NNRTIs.
evidence: The claim is based on structural analysis and comparison.

claim: Mutations of Pro225 and Pro236, whose side chains interact with the right wing of 25a, but not that of RPV, do not cause resistance to 25a.
source: Although it potentially makes K-5a2 and 25a susceptible to mutations of the residues not contacted by ETR or RPV, our results have shown that mutations of Pro225 and Pro236, whose side chains interact with the right wing of 25a, but not that of RPV, do not cause resistance to 25a.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript (Table 2).

claim: The mutations of Lys104 and Val106 are unlikely to cause loss of potency of 25a because the two hydrogen bonds between 25a and these residues are established through the main chains of Lys104 and Val106.
source: Additional RT-25a interactions that are not present in the RT/RPV complex include the hydrogen bonds between the sulfonamide group of 25a and Lys104 and Val106. The mutations of these two residues are unlikely to cause loss of potency of 25a because the two hydrogen bonds are established through the main chains of Lys104 and Val106.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis.

claim: Even if the side-chain substitutions of Lys104 and Val106 deviate the main chains, a minor change in the torsion angle τ1 would readily place the sulfonamide group of 25a in an optimal position for hydrogen bonds formation.
source: Even if the side-chain substitutions deviate the main chains, a minor change in the torsion angle τ1, which was shown to span a wide range without significant energetic penalty (Table 5), would readily place the sulfonamide group of 25a in an optimal position for hydrogen bonds formation.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from structural analysis and energy calculations (Table 5).

claim: The findings provide a reliable model to analyze the structural effects of drug-resistant mutations in RT.
source: Our findings provide a reliable model to analyze the structural effects of drug-resistant mutations in RT
evidence: The claim is a summary statement based on the structural data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The findings will contribute to structure-based design of novel NNRTIs that can effectively target multiple variants of RT.
